To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Mn(4+) → Mn(3+) transition is accompanied with the change of the oxidation states of neighboring oxygen atoms, (2) the Mn(3+) → Mn(4+) transition is accompanied by the emptying of 3d(z2 ) states, (3) the activation energy for the Mn(4+)-to-Mn(3+) transition on the λ-Mn(2) (001) surface is 0.12eV.
the surface reconstruction of the λ-MO(2) (001) (where M is Mn, Fe, or Co) leads to the formation of the Mn(3+) cations with a local coordination number of four.

the surface reconstruction of λ-MnO2(001) leads to a transition from Mn(4+), Mn(3+) and Mn(4+) oxidation states, and the reconstruction proceeds via a transition state with Mn(4+)-Mn(3+) and two adjacent O atoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure of the surface of a new layered manganite λ-MnO2.
the electronic structure of the reconstructed λ-MnO2(001) surface and the origin of its catalytic activity.
the structural and electronic properties of reconstructed λ-MnO2(001) surface and their influence on the catalytic performance of this material in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface of λ-MnO2 is reconstructed and this reconstruction is accompanied by a change of the Mn oxidation state.
the surface reconstruction is not the reason for the Mn(3+) formation at the λ-Mn(2)O(3)(001) surface, but rather a consequence of it.
the surface reconstruction is not a spontaneous one and it is not a necessary condition for the Mn reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface of MnO(2) can be reduced to Mn(3) by the reconstruction, and this is a spontaneous process at the temperature of 300 K.

the surface reconstruction of λ-MnO (2)(001) is driven by a change of the Mn oxidation state from + 4 to + 3, and the reconstruction is not a spontaneous reaction, but requires an activation energy of about 0.12eV.
the surface reconstruction is a possible mechanism for the transition from Mn(4 + ) to Mn(3 + ) in the bulk.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the λ-Mn(3+) O(2) reconstruction of the MnO(2)(100) surface can be induced by an external agent, such as a reducing agent or a high temperature, which leads to the change of the Mn oxidation state from +2 to +3.
the surface reconstruction at the (001) surface of layered manganites can be used as a tool to induce a transition from a high-spin Mn(4+) (S = 3/2) to a low-spin Mn(3+) (S =1/2).
the surface Mn(3+)-O(2) bond is much weaker than that of Mn(4+)-O(4) bond.
